annotation.title_clean: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.title_en: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.venue: International Labour Organization (ILO Voices / Future of Work Podcast page)
annotation.summary_en: ILO policy brief by Berg and Gmyrek examining how large language models such as ChatGPT affect knowledge workers. It argues task transformation and job quality matter more than job losses, highlights the digital divide and precarious data-labelling work, and calls for social dialogue, occupational safety and health protections, and regulation of new AI-related occupations.
key_provisions_or_claims: Between 644 and 997 million knowledge workers globally (19.6-30.4% of employment) are potentially exposed to LLMs
LLMs are more likely to transform tasks than replace whole jobs
Job quality, not only job quantity, must be a policy focus
Data-labelling workers training AI face precarious conditions and psychosocial risks requiring OSH regulation
Social dialogue should be used from the outset when technology is designed and adopted
